title: Last-marker stripping with bounded space
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$ of length $n$, $M$ halts within $c(n+1)^2$ steps. It outputs the pair encoding of $a$ and the prefix of $v$ strictly before its last $1$ when $x$ parses into $(a,v)$ by the aligned-pair parser and $v$ contains a $1$; otherwise it outputs the empty word. For every Boolean word $x$ and every time $t$, the computation of $M$ on $x$ up to time $t$ uses at most $c(|x|+1)$ work-tape cells.
